I am a 55-year-old woman farming in the South East, and this 0.05-hectare plot behind my compound is where I grow cassava and cocoyam intercropped with a little maize. Because the plot is small and owned by my household, I will work it with my own family labor and feed the soil with compost and poultry droppings I have saved; I will not spend money on chemical fertilizer or improved seeds because they are too costly for such a small piece of land, and the rains here are enough without irrigation. I will also not spray any chemicals, as we do not usually do that for root crops around here.
